en: The Philippine tarsier has enormous eyes that are actually larger than its brain to help it hunt insects at night.
The endangered Nepenthes attenboroughii pitcher plant grows only on the summit of Mount Victoria in Palawan and traps insects for food.
The tamaraw is a dwarf buffalo endemic to Mindoro that has distinctive V-shaped horns and is critically endangered.
The Aedes aegypti mosquito transmits dengue fever in the Philippines by biting humans during the early morning and late afternoon.
The Philippines is part of the Coral Triangle, which contains the highest diversity of marine fish and coral species on Earth.
Rice, or palay, is a monocotyledonous grass that grows in flooded paddies and serves as the main staple food for Filipinos.
The Philippine eagle is a critically endangered apex predator that hunts flying foxes and monitor lizards in the forests of Mindanao.
Female golden kuhol snails lay bright pink egg masses on rice plant stems above the water to protect them from aquatic predators.
The carabao wallows in mud during hot afternoons because it lacks functional sweat glands and needs the mud to cool its body.
Calamansi fruits are rich in vitamin C, which helps Filipino children produce collagen and maintain a healthy immune system.
Mangrove forests in places like Palawan have specialized stilt roots that filter salt and protect coastal communities from strong typhoon storm surges.
The Luzon giant cloud rat lives in high-altitude mossy forests and has thick fur to adapt to the cold, cloudy mountain environment.
